## behavior

### Analysing Instead Of Attuning
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's own example, and an unusually candid one: an entire earlier career built on personality models, so that everyone she met could be placed on the right axes. It felt like attunement because she was attuned — to the image of the person assembled in her head. In the room she was half present, measuring what was said against the models. For someone else the frame might be good person or bad, competent or not; the effect is the same.

  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=700)
  - contrasts_with → Presence And Curiosity Versus Strategy And Analysis (https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=740)
  - mirrors → Using The Framework As An Excuse (https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=760)
  - source: Attunement: How Securely Attached People Develop Intimacy @700s — https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=700

### Asking Whether They Like You Instead Of Whether You Like Them
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Through the dating phase the running questions are whether you are acceptable to them yet, and how to get them to commit. What goes unasked is whether you like this person, whether they fit your life, whether your futures point the same way. Priebe's point is that the omission does not stay hidden — it surfaces later, as the conflict phase, once the securing is done.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=640)
  - mirrors → Fixating On Whether They Like You (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=620)
  - contrasts_with → Owning Who You Pursue (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=700)
  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles In Relationships @640s — https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=640

### Auditing The Timeline
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Stopping on the gaps and contradictions in a partner's account. From inside, this is the avoidant route to changing a feeling — reconstruct what caused it and the state becomes manageable. From the anxious side it lands as a verdict that the feeling is unearned, which is the moment the conversation stops being about the original hurt.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/GE0iRhskMW8?t=310)
  - mistaken_for → Minimizing What You Are Going Through (https://youtu.be/GE0iRhskMW8?t=380)
  - contrasts_with → Acknowledging The Feeling, Not The Logic (https://youtu.be/GE0iRhskMW8?t=400)
  - source: Why Does The Anxious Attachment Style Exaggerate? @310s — https://youtu.be/GE0iRhskMW8?t=310

### Best Behaviour To Get Back In
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Agreeing, at the door, to the amount of space that broke you last time — and knowing in your gut that in six months it will not hold. Priebe says we always know when we are doing this, and names it as a boundary violation in its own right rather than optimism: the other person is being enrolled in a plan on terms you have privately not accepted.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=660)
  - mistaken_for → Honest Expression Of Need (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=700)
  - contrasts_with → Agreeing Expectations Explicitly (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=780)
  - source: Anxious Attachment: 5 Questions To Ask Yourself Before Getting Back Together With An Ex @660s — https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=660

### Burying The Episode
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Filing an incident somewhere you have agreed with yourself never to look. Priebe describes doing this for years with something that turned out, once examined, to need only an apology — the guilt underneath had been unreachable because shame arrived first every time the memory surfaced.

  - contrasts_with → Checking Whether It Pulls You In Or Out (https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=660)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=690)

### Confiding In Friends Not The Partner
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The most legible symptom she offers: the people around you knowing more about your frustrations, doubts and private verdicts on your partner than your partner does. In a relationship running in good faith, the partner is the best-informed person about how you feel toward them.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1443)
  - source: The Real Reason Why Most Anxious-Avoidant Relationships Fail (And How To Combat It) @1443s — https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1443

### Decoding An Indirect Partner
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Working out what someone means rather than asking them — a skill built early in a home where people were not direct, and then kept in use by choosing partners who are not either. She notes the tell: the friends get consulted about what the partner is thinking, and the partner does not.

  - triggers → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=647)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=647)

### Defensiveness
*behavior · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

What fight-or-flight looks like inside a conversation. She is even-handed that this is not style-specific — everyone does it under threat, and attachment style only decides its shape.

  - source: Cultivating The Ability To Tolerate Emotional Discomfort @70s — https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=70

### Dictating The Solution
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Coming to the conversation with the answer already decided. It can be a good answer and still fail, either because it is not workable for the other person or because they will carry it out while resentment accumulates underneath.

### Emotional Withdrawal
*behavior · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The visible end of deactivation: less contact, less disclosure, less of oneself brought into the room. Usually read by the other person as a verdict, when it is closer to a reflex.

### Escalating Anger
*behavior · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The fight side of the same strategy: making the failure impossible to ignore. She notes it can present as cool and controlled rather than loud — an adult version of a toddler's protest, aimed at the same result.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=430)
  - contrasts_with → Escalating Vulnerability (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=551)

### Escalating Vulnerability
*behavior · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

One of the two channels she describes, the fawn side: showing the other person how much you need them so that caring for you becomes the obvious thing to do. In adults it grows more sophisticated but keeps the same shape.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=430)
  - mistaken_for → Honest Expression Of Need (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=551)

### Exonerating The Caregiver
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Naming something as harm means saying your feelings were caused by someone else, which is precisely the move this system cannot make. So the past gets recalled as untroubled and even serious mistreatment is reframed as having been deserved or useful — which is also why avoidant adults often cannot locate where their attachment style came from.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=961)
  - source: How Does An Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @961s — https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=961

### Fixating On The Partner's Flaws
*behavior · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Once the threat program is running, flaws are what get logged. Her comparison is being chased through a forest: the scenery is still beautiful, but nobody being chased is looking at it.

  - triggers → Loss Of Attraction (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=607)

### Fixating On Whether They Like You
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious tell for the same moderate range, and a genuinely useful diagnostic: a sudden preoccupation with whether someone is annoyed with you usually means distress has risen somewhere in your life, not necessarily in that relationship. Attention has simply been trained to go looking for closeness whenever the level climbs.

  - triggers → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=965)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=965)
  - source: Attachment & Nervous System Wiring 101: How Childhood Shapes Your Thinking and Self-Regulation @965s — https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=965

### Forcing Your Inner State To Conform
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The avoidant tell for moderate distress: growing frustrated that you cannot perform at the level you have decided is required, and treating your own depletion as a discipline problem. Rest gets measured against an external standard — eight hours, therefore rested — while the body's actual signal is overruled.

  - triggers → Burnout Collapse (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=1449)
  - mirrors → Fixating On Whether They Like You (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=1449)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=1449)
  - source: Attachment & Nervous System Wiring 101: How Childhood Shapes Your Thinking and Self-Regulation @1449s — https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=1449

### Gaslighting Yourself About Anger
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Meeting each small irritation with an internal ruling that it does not warrant a response. Priebe notes the voice is still there for her, and that its favourite argument — this is too small to bring up — is precisely inverted: smallness is what makes a thing tractable.

  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=280)
  - contrasts_with → Expressing Anger At Two Out Of Ten (https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=500)

### Getting Lost In The Story
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Spending the afternoon narrating the sadness rather than having it, which keeps re-summoning the feeling into the body. Her instruction is to check the body before the mind, since the story is usually running before anyone notices it started.

  - triggers → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=891)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=891)
  - source: Learning Self-Regulation Through Self-Attunement @891s — https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=891

### Honest Expression Of Need
*behavior · synthesis · secure=secure-form*

Saying what you need plainly, which requires first being in contact with it and able to name it. It is what escalation is a substitute for, and it only becomes possible once needs can be consistently met rather than intermittently extracted.

  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @1326s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1326
  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1326)

### Ignoring People As A Boundary
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

She closes on this: avoidant people often believe boundaries are their strength, when what they are doing is disengaging without ever stating a limit. Withdrawal and a boundary can look identical from outside and differ completely in whether the other person was told anything.

  - mistaken_for → Boundary (https://youtu.be/9WzGv5SNgBQ?t=655)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/9WzGv5SNgBQ?t=655)

### Insisting You Were Right
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Giving bad directions and then maintaining they were good, with the other person's navigation offered as the explanation. The cost is not the original error — it is that the person's own instrument stops being trustworthy to them.

  - triggers → Identity Threat (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=962)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=962)
  - source: Early Experiences Of The Secure Attachment Style @962s — https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=962

### Introducing Old Grievances
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Older incidents arriving mid-conflict as further evidence. She reads most of them as stand-ins for the present feeling rather than the real subject — and notes that agreeing to a specific time to discuss one often settles it, because what was needed was the knowledge that you would.

  - triggers → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=1044)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=1044)

### Letting A Relationship Go
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary · sign of change*

A sign of change rather than a loss: recognising a relationship where what you need is not on offer, and stopping — without the frantic push to get the person to see it differently. She frames the inner work as only half of it; the other half is making your surroundings match.

  - contrasts_with → Pursuing Inconsistent Partners (https://youtu.be/HHJ1dKAL18Y?t=123)
  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/HHJ1dKAL18Y?t=123)
  - source: 5 Struggles Securely Attached People Still Have @123s — https://youtu.be/HHJ1dKAL18Y?t=123

### Letting The Pain Land
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating · sign of change*

A sign of change: registering the cost of an interaction while it is happening rather than reconstructing it later without the charge. Her point is that this is where boundaries come from — pain is the instrument that tells you what to avoid, and without it you can only conclude that everything is survivable.

  - contrasts_with → Pain Hidden From Yourself (https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=966)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: The Blindspot That Keeps You Repeating The Same Relationship Mistakes @966s — https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=966

### Looking Down On The Partner
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Contempt made operational. Writing the other person off as incapable removes the need to be vulnerable with them — and removes their chance to do better, because they are no longer being handed anything real to meet.

  - triggers → The Partner's Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092)

### Loving Too Hard
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Her sharpest reframe in this video, and an uncomfortable one. Persisting with someone who has said what they want, when it is not you, is not an excess of generosity — it is declining to take their answer. Giving to someone not asking to receive looks like devotion from inside and like a boundary being crossed from outside.

  - mistaken_for → Honest Expression Of Need (https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=122)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=122)
  - triggers → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=122)
  - source: Anxious Attachment: 3 Early Signs Of Healing @122s — https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=122

### Making It A Relationship Issue
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Rather than saying this matters to me, saying that it is important for a relationship — which is harder to refuse and cannot be rejected personally. Priebe's objection is what it costs: dressing a want as a principle also removes the chance of the want itself being seen and taken seriously.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=520)
  - contrasts_with → Honest Expression Of Need (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=540)
  - mistaken_for → Framing It As A Shared Problem (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=530)
  - source: Anxious Attachment: How to Find Your INNER ADULT When Triggered @520s — https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=520

### Manufacturing A Reason For The Feeling
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

If raw feeling will not be taken seriously, the anxious partner supplies a rationale that will. Priebe's example: irritation at a partner newly working from home, unexplained, gets recast as worry about money and the mortgage — and now the couple is having a detailed conversation on a level where the problem does not exist. The real one was needing time alone.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=850)
  - mirrors → Exaggerating The Story (https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=830)
  - contrasts_with → Bringing The Feeling Without An Explanation (https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=950)
  - source: Top 10 Mistakes Anxious/Avoidant Couples Make (And How To Fix Them) @850s — https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=850

### Minimizing What You Are Going Through
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Reflexively shrinking the account of what is happening to you, often past the point of plausibility. She notes the social cost is usually misread: people conclude you are unfriendly or uninterested, when what they are seeing is someone managing another person's concern away.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=651)
  - triggers → Self-Disgust At Your Own Need (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=651)
  - mistaken_for → Ignoring People As A Boundary (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=651)
  - source: Why Does The Avoidant Attachment Style Fear Intimacy? @651s — https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=651

### Mistaking Attraction For A Decision
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

For most people attraction is a yellow light — reason to find out more. For the anxious system it settles the question. Priebe notes what does not then happen: the getting-to-know-you that would establish whether this person fits a life, because the enquiry has already moved on to how to be wanted by them.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=500)
  - mistaken_for → Chosen Excitement (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=510)
  - contrasts_with → Reviewing The Relationship Objectively (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=530)
  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles In Relationships @500s — https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=500

### Naming The Fantasy
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating · sign of change*

A sign of change: spotting the invented version while it is running, and letting the real person be disappointing rather than treating the gap as something they owe you. She puts it plainly — you do not get to be angry at someone for not following a script they were never shown.

  - contrasts_with → Limerence (https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=321)
  - source: Anxious Attachment: 3 Early Signs Of Healing @321s — https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=321

### Partner Stops Rising To The Occasion
*behavior · the partner's side · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The other half of the loop. Handed no real responsibility and no honest account of what hurt, the partner has nothing to respond to competently — which is then read as confirmation that they never could.

  - triggers → Unregistered Hurt (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @1092s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092

### Pursuing Inconsistent Partners
*behavior · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Saying, sincerely, that what you want is someone emotionally available, and then not pursuing them when they appear. The responsive partner does not register as the thing being searched for.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=430)
  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @430s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=430

### Putting People On Pedestals
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Her example is imagining a rich inner life in a reserved partner and growing frustrated when it does not surface. The corrective she offers is a sorting question worth asking often: what did this person actually tell me or show me, and what did I supply on their behalf?

  - triggers → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=970)
  - part_of → Negative View Of Self, Positive View Of Others (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=970)

### Putting Your Own Needs Aside
*behavior · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Setting down what you need in order to attend to someone else's difficulty. Done once it is generosity; done as a standing position it accrues a debt the other person never agreed to.

  - triggers → Resentment (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=374)
  - source: Attachment Styles & The Drama Triangle (Part 1): Intro To The Drama Triangle @374s — https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=374

### Recognizing Your Own Vulnerability
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating · sign of change*

A sign of change: locating the places, past or present, where you needed care and did not get it — without first requiring a justification for why it counts. She describes it as recognising impact regardless of circumstance.

  - contrasts_with → Everything That Happens Is My Doing (https://youtu.be/ssB6tsIxlls?t=256)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: 3 Early Signs Of Healing @256s — https://youtu.be/ssB6tsIxlls?t=256

### Refining The Ideal Partner
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The failure loop she describes: leave a bad relationship, get more specific about the traits to avoid, and find each successive partnership contains less of the bad without ever becoming the good one. The work feels like progress and is really goalpost movement, because the search is still for someone who will do the protecting.

  - triggers → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/VBJyaBy_kxQ?t=607)
  - part_of → The Deflated Wheel (https://youtu.be/VBJyaBy_kxQ?t=607)

*behavior · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The return, which restores the closeness — and with it the conditions that started the sequence.

### Rushing To Depth
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Needing every conversation to reach the core immediately, and finding anything lighter unbearable. Her analogy is compulsive eating: someone who eats without attention is not savouring food, whatever their enthusiasm for it — and the same distinction separates savouring closeness from consuming it.

  - part_of → Enmeshment (https://youtu.be/GGEty6uo9Nc?t=122)

### Scanning For Confirmation
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Searching the partner for any small indication that the feared thing is true — and finding one, because a search that specific always does. What was a fear then arrives back as confirmed knowledge.

  - triggers → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1086)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1086)

### Self-Punishment Instead Of Amends
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Going through enough private misery about something that it starts to feel settled. Priebe's correction is blunt: the harm done to the other person does not decrease by any amount of self-hatred. Shame is so consuming that it crowds out the other person's perspective entirely, which is exactly the perspective repair requires.

  - mistaken_for → Naming Hurt And Repairing (https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=500)

### Stating A Surface Grievance
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The complaint offered in conflict, which is sincerely meant and is not the operative one. Her paired examples: the avoidant partner wanting to avoid drama, where what is being avoided is the exposure of saying what they need; the anxious partner wanting things to be alright, where what is urgent is the return of co-regulation.

  - source: The Real Reason Why Most Anxious-Avoidant Relationships Fail (And How To Combat It) @577s — https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=577

### Suppressing The Other Side
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Entering the next relationship determined to keep the unwanted half out of sight. It works for a while, which is the problem — the partner meets it later and with less warning, so it lands harder. She describes the result as an escalating cycle: each attempt to hide it better produces more chaos when the lid finally comes off.

  - triggers → Approach-Avoidance Conflict (https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=728)
  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=728)

### Suppressing Your Needs Early
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Declining to state a want at the point where stating it feels most dangerous. Sometimes the need is actively disclaimed out loud, which is what makes it land as a change of terms rather than a disclosure when it surfaces later.

  - part_of → Accidental Bad Faith (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=459)

### Telling The Story Instead Of Naming The Feeling
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Producing a vivid account designed to induce an emotional reaction rather than saying the emotion outright. Priebe reads this as the safer of two moves: the story can be argued with, but naming the feeling and the need directly exposes them, so the story goes first.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/GE0iRhskMW8?t=520)

### The Outer Critic Quieting
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating · sign of change*

Other people's visible need stops registering as an offence. She is precise that this does not require agreeing with them — you may still think a display is overdone — only that it no longer lands at the level of anger, because the rule it was breaking has loosened in you.

  - contrasts_with → The Outer Critic (https://youtu.be/ZvqnHlHlqzM?t=486)

### Using The Framework As An Excuse
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The other misuse, and the mirror of the first: taking the diagnosis as a licence rather than a starting point. Her two examples are being owed an unusual amount of reassurance, and being exempt from caring how others feel. Both convert an explanation of where a pattern came from into a reason it should be accommodated.

  - mirrors → Using The Framework To Manipulate (https://youtu.be/vlL6L7Cck-c?t=601)

### Using The Framework To Manipulate
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The misuse she calls the largest online: learning someone's style in order to route around what they have said they want. Her argument is that the move is self-defeating on its own terms — attempting to override another person's stated wishes is itself an insecure response, and security is precisely the capacity to take someone at face value. She notes recovery programmes carry an explicit rule against using their own language this way, for the same reason.

  - mistaken_for → Taking Your Partner At Face Value (https://youtu.be/vlL6L7Cck-c?t=241)
  - contrasts_with → Honest Expression Of Need (https://youtu.be/vlL6L7Cck-c?t=361)
  - source: How Not To Use Attachment Theory @241s — https://youtu.be/vlL6L7Cck-c?t=241

### Venting Instead Of Being Vulnerable
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe separates seeking support from building a case. Describing your partner as terrible so a friend will say leave them is not the vulnerable version; the vulnerable version is saying you do not know how to fix it, that you are in pain, that you are afraid of being told to leave, and that you are not ready to. The first keeps the shame intact; only the second gets you anything.

  - mistaken_for → Confiding In Friends Not The Partner (https://youtu.be/-PCcJsp30AA?t=1210)
  - contrasts_with → Comfort From Someone Other Than The One Who Hurt You (https://youtu.be/-PCcJsp30AA?t=1230)
  - source: Fearful-Avoidants: Breaking The Cycle Of On-Again Off-Again Relationships @1210s — https://youtu.be/-PCcJsp30AA?t=1210

### Waiting Out The Activated State
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core · sign of change*

A sign of change rather than a symptom: noticing that the system is pulling in several directions at once, and treating that as a reason not to act rather than a reason to act urgently.

What the top of the scale looks like on the avoidant side, and the exact counterpart of self-abandonment on the anxious side. Where one system will cross its own limits to secure comfort, this one will burn itself down to stop registering discomfort at all.

*state · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A background dread of being left that stays conscious rather than surfacing only in crises. She locates its intensity precisely: it persists because the person does not know they would be alright on their own, never having learned to bring themselves back to equilibrium without help.

### Contempt
*state · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

What arrives in place of the vulnerable feeling. Contempt is functional: someone you look down on is someone you will not depend on or be soft with, so it enforces the distance that makes further hurt unlikely.

### Curiosity And Appreciation
*state · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The state the system runs before anything is at stake: noticing what is attractive, interesting and compatible about someone. It is not an illusion later corrected — it is accurate perception that a threat response subsequently crowds out.

### Desensitization To One's Own Emotions
*state · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The long-run result of a brain that stopped attending to feelings it found useless. It often becomes visible only at a death or a breakup, when the person can see that a strong feeling is warranted and cannot locate it in themselves. She is explicit that this is not an absence of empathy — it is insensitivity to one's own signal, not other people's.

  - healed_by → Re-Sensitizing To Your Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=349)

### Disgust At Displayed Vulnerability
*state · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The strong repulsion many avoidant adults feel watching someone else exaggerate need, sadness or vulnerability — often with an edge of rage when that display is rewarded. It is the refused-currency injustice surfacing, and it points precisely at which emotions were made shameful in them.

### Emotional Dysregulation
*state · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Either a response far larger than the present occasion warrants — the past arriving in the body and being mistaken for now — or a diffuse offness with no locatable cause. The second kind is harder for insecurely attached people, since there is nothing to attune to without knowing what is being felt or why.

### Emotional Flashback
*state · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The activated anxious state read as a flashback rather than a mood. Some part of the system is filing the situation exactly as it did in childhood — I cannot meet my own needs, so my only route is making my distress unmissable to this person. Technically untrue for an adult with money, friends and skills, and completely convincing from inside, because the part running it cannot access how old you are.

### Existential Loneliness
*state · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Not the ordinary version — nobody in my life currently sees me — but a felt certainty that being seen and known is not a thing that can happen. Priebe traces it to a sense of self that formed largely without mirroring, and compounds it: where a phobia of inner experience has left parts of you unvisited, the sense that you cannot be fully known is also accurate.

*state · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The avoidant counterpart to abandonment fear, and just as chronic and low-level: that someone will arrive, require everything, and leave nothing of you. It is why being told you must change to make someone happy lands so much harder here than the content of the request warrants.

*state · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The recognition that something you did landed badly on someone else — which requires already knowing that their experience is not yours. Priebe treats it as the more useful of the two feelings: it is a self-monitoring signal that points at a specific action and at a specific person, and it can be acted on.

### Guilt At Wanting Space
*state · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The other arm. Enmeshment patterning says that being in a relationship means giving your partner everything and caretaking without interruption, so any move toward your own separateness registers as a moral failure. Priebe finds fearful-avoidants the most caretaking of the styles, and reads the guilt as what eventually forces the exit — the only permitted route to solitude is out.

The state where a disagreement stops being about its subject and becomes about whether you are a certain kind of person. Once it is on, the system is in self-protection and the argument cannot resolve, because resolving it is no longer what is being attempted.

The other half of the oscillation. Alone, with nothing to be threatened by, the wish for closeness returns in full and often as fantasy — which is why she says this system can tolerate intimacy best precisely when it is not available.

*state · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The mechanism underneath the layer everyone gets wrong. The fear is not that the other person will reject the disclosure — it is that disclosing triggers rejection from inside. Available from roughly fifteen months, well before a child understands that it and its caregiver are separate people — which is why an unreturned bid does not register as rejection but as the self coming apart. Looking back from a deactivated state at what was expressed while activated, and finding both the expression and the underlying feeling shameful — particularly if the other person received it badly. What being treated as incompetent does to the person on the receiving end. Nobody regulates well while being handled as someone who cannot be trusted with responsibility.

  - manifests_as → Partner Stops Rising To The Occasion (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @1092s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092

### Unmetabolised Grief
*state · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A loss that was never felt because the system would not release it into awareness. Priebe describes avoidant people who felt nothing at a death and are still, years later, triggered by things they cannot connect to it, or whose physical and mental health declines around material the body has been holding without ever handing over.

  - originates_in → Unprocessable Emotion In The Caregiver (https://youtu.be/_UVZHhWTX5Y?t=150)
  - healed_by → Re-Sensitizing To Your Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/_UVZHhWTX5Y?t=265)

### Unregistered Hurt
*state · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Hurt that occurred and was processed defensively rather than felt. It still has to go somewhere, so it surfaces as a stance toward the other person rather than as pain.

  - manifests_as → Looking Down On The Partner (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=970)

## strategy

### Affect Suppression
*strategy · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The system does not merely hide hurt from other people — it withholds the experience from the person having it. Where reaching out was historically met with hostility, the body learns to cut the feeling off before it reaches awareness, and something more defensible surfaces in its place.

  - originates_in → Attachment-Seeking Met With Hostility (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=850)
  - deactivates → Unregistered Hurt (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=970)

  - mirrors → Amplifying The Signal (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=309)
  - manifests_as → Stating A Surface Grievance (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=577)
  - part_of → Pain Hidden From Yourself (https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=482)

### Amplifying The Signal
*strategy · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The mechanism behind hyperactivation. Because emotional display worked intermittently rather than never, the child learned that display is worth doing — and that when it fails, the correct adjustment is more of it.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=309)
  - mirrors → Affect Suppression (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=309)
  - manifests_as → Escalating Vulnerability (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=430)

  - originates_in → Inconsistent Responsiveness (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=309)
  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @309s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=309

### Automatic Redirect To Solution
*strategy · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The moment a difficult feeling appears, attention reroutes to what would resolve the situation. Priebe is careful that this is not a decision not to dwell — the redirect happens before the feeling is fully registered, which is why sitting with it later is so hard to do on request.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/4avJofwpVNw?t=390)
  - manifests_as → Dictating The Solution (https://youtu.be/4avJofwpVNw?t=400)

  - source: Anxious vs Avoidant Attachment Styles & Emotional Pain @390s — https://youtu.be/4avJofwpVNw?t=390

### Becoming What They Want
*strategy · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The unspoken arrangement she describes: be the person they seem to want until they are secured, and raise your own needs afterwards. It works, briefly, and it guarantees the conflict that follows — because the needs arriving later were never part of what the other person agreed to.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=459)
  - manifests_as → Suppressing Your Needs Early (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=459)

  - source: 10 Signs You May Have An Anxious Attachment Style @459s — https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=459

### Deactivating Strategies
*strategy · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The avoidant threat response. Once the body registers that it has grown dependent on someone, the system stops running the program that noticed what it liked about them and starts running one that scans for cost. Attraction does not fade at random — it goes offline because attention has been redirected.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=2)
  - mirrors → Hyperactivating Strategies (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=365)

  - originates_in → Attachment-Seeking Met With Hostility (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=850)
  - contrasts_with → Holding Both Programs (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1333)
  - healed_by → Tracking What You Receive (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1212)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @2s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=2

### Environmental Control
*strategy · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A whole life quietly arranged so that mood stays predictable without anyone else's involvement. Her examples are a fixed early-morning routine, or always having a next trip or venture in view — small reliable comforts that never depend on another person. Almost none of it is consciously understood as regulation.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=96)
  - regulates → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=217)

  - part_of → It Does Not Occur To Them (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=96)

### Exaggerating The Story
*strategy · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Turning up the events so the listener will arrive at the right feeling. Priebe is explicit that this is not deception in the ordinary sense: the emotion being reported is real and undistorted, and the facts are being bent in service of transmitting it. Which is also why calling it out as exaggeration reliably produces more of it.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/GE0iRhskMW8?t=250)

### Hyperactivating Strategies
*strategy · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious counterpart. The same growing dependency that sends the avoidant system scanning for cost sends this one scanning for signs the bond is at risk, because what it cannot afford to lose is the co-regulation itself.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=365)

### Keeping The Upper Hand
*strategy · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Selecting someone you quietly believe could never fully understand you, which keeps control where it feels safe. She points out the trap: since your own needs are hidden from you as well, no partner could meet them, and the resulting disappointment then confirms the choice.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1187)
  - defends_against → Vulnerability Leads To Rejection (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1187)

### Monitoring The Bond
*strategy · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Continuous surveillance of the relationship for small shifts in the partner's warmth or responsiveness, on the reasoning that the reassurance you depend on could be withdrawn without notice.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=846)

### Persecutor Position
*strategy · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The same conviction of having been wronged, delivered forcefully rather than plaintively: here is what you did, here is what you must change. She notes the illusion in it — it feels powerful precisely because it is direct, while still leaving your equilibrium contingent on someone else's compliance.

  - part_of → The Drama Triangle (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=254)
  - manifests_as → Defensiveness (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=254)

  - source: Attachment Styles And The Drama Triangle (Part 2) @1100s — https://youtu.be/ynMNRFp68LM?t=1100

### Preemptive Sabotage
*strategy · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

If something is certain to go wrong, going first is the only move that returns any control. What looks like destroying a good relationship is the system acting on a prediction it has never had reason to doubt.

  - manifests_as → Breaking It Off (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=502)
  - defends_against → Pursue But Never Relax (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=382)

  - source: How Does A Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @502s — https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=502

### Projecting The Intolerable Feeling
*strategy · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

When a feeling cannot be processed — shame above all — it is relocated to someone else, because a feeling that belongs to another person is one they can be recruited to fix. Her example: the self-disgust in the mirror becomes a search for proof the partner finds you disgusting. It is not experienced as invention; it feels like accurate knowledge of what they think.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1086)
  - manifests_as → Scanning For Confirmation (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1086)
  - mirrors → Rationalizing The Feeling Away (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1086)
  - healed_by → Owning The Feeling As Yours (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1206)
  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @1086s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1086
  - contrasts_with → Differentiation (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=966)

### Rationalizing The Feeling Away
*strategy · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The adult mechanism: scan the environment for a justification, and if none is blatant enough, conclude the feeling itself is mistaken. Emotion is admitted only once it has passed an evidentiary test.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=470)
  - deactivates → Desensitization To One's Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=470)

### Resource Threat Scanning
*strategy · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

What the avoidant system starts doing once attachment comes online: auditing the relationship for what it will cost. Is this person independent enough, will they take time from what keeps me regulated, how do they reflect on me. The scan is not malice — it is a threat response aimed at protecting self-sufficiency.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=486)
  - deactivates → Curiosity And Appreciation (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=607)
  - manifests_as → Fixating On The Partner's Flaws (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=607)
  - defends_against → Depending On Others Costs Me Myself (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=486)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @486s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=486

### Saviour Position
*strategy · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Seeking out people who seem to need fixing and setting your own needs aside for them. It reads as generosity and functions as dependency-building — and it carries an unspoken contract that the care will be repaid, which is what makes the slide into feeling wronged almost inevitable.

  - part_of → The Drama Triangle (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=374)
  - manifests_as → Putting Your Own Needs Aside (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=374)
  - healed_by → Taking The Coach Position (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=555)

  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/ynMNRFp68LM?t=1840)
  - source: Attachment Styles And The Drama Triangle (Part 2) @1840s — https://youtu.be/ynMNRFp68LM?t=1840

### Sequence Analysis
*strategy · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The avoidant over-inflated wheel: learning early that understanding why something happened mattered more than processing how it felt, and getting very good at it. A finished relationship gets reviewed as a sequence — this interaction produced that fight, my move produced their counter-move — often with real accuracy about one's own part. She rates the skill highly and says secure people use it constantly; the problem is running it alone.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=122)
  - part_of → The Deflated Wheel (https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=122)
  - mirrors → Openness Without Self-Protection (https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=242)
  - contrasts_with → Treating Emotion As Data (https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=362)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: The Blindspot That Keeps You Repeating The Same Relationship Mistakes @122s — https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=122

### The Fawn Response After A Rupture
*strategy · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The urge to go straight to the apology is not repair — Priebe reads it as the fourth branch of fight, flight and freeze, running the same short-term threat response. It resolves the immediate danger to the relationship and does nothing about the pattern, which is what the next conversation will need.

  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=690)
  - manifests_as → Putting Your Own Needs Aside (https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=700)
  - healed_by → Naming It Before Apologising (https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=350)
  - source: What To Do When You Mess Up (Attachment Healing) @690s — https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=690

### The Outer Critic
*strategy · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A rule internalised about yourself, then enforced outwards. Where showing need was not permitted, other people showing it reads as a rule being broken rather than as their business. Her image for it is the two-year-old's sense of fairness: if I cannot have the toy, nobody may.

  - originates_in → Attachment-Seeking Met With Hostility (https://youtu.be/ZvqnHlHlqzM?t=365)
  - healed_by → Reading Disgust As A Map (https://youtu.be/ZvqnHlHlqzM?t=365)
  - defends_against → Vulnerability Leads To Rejection (https://youtu.be/ZvqnHlHlqzM?t=365)
  - source: Fearful-Avoidant Attachment: 3 Early Signs Of Healing @365s — https://youtu.be/ZvqnHlHlqzM?t=365

### The Social Mask
*strategy · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Most fearful-avoidant people spend more time in one response than the other, and build an identity on it — the analytical one, or the selfless and giving one — while carrying quiet embarrassment about the other. She traces the choice to whichever worked in early life, and notes the cost: the presented self is a genuine half of the person, sold as the whole.

  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=485)
  - defends_against → I Am Not Okay And Neither Are You (https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=485)

  - healed_by → Sensitizing, Then Sharing (https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=1332)
  - source: Fearful-Avoidant: The Blindspot That Keeps You Repeating The Same Relationship Mistakes @485s — https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=485

### Victim Position
*strategy · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Entering conflict as the one things happen to: I did not cause this, so I cannot and should not be the one to fix it. It runs on a real appetite for justice, and it hands your wellbeing to whoever you are waiting on.

  - part_of → The Drama Triangle (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=254)

## trigger

### Broken Promise
*trigger · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A concrete instance of hurt that does not get registered: someone says they will do something and does not. The pain is real, and a conclusion about the person's reliability arrives in place of it.

  - triggers → Unregistered Hurt (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=970)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @970s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=970

### Growing Dependency
*trigger · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The threshold that brings the attachment system online. It rarely announces itself: the body simply gets used to someone being reachable and starts predicting their availability. Everything downstream follows from that prediction, not from a decision.

  - triggers → Resource Threat Scanning (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=245)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @245s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=245

### Relationship Escalation
*trigger · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Deactivation is not confined to the start of a relationship. Any event that rearranges how much room the relationship takes up — moving in, a child, a partner suddenly home all day — can bring the same response online years later.

  - triggers → Resource Threat Scanning (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=728)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @728s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=728

### Things Going Well
*trigger · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The signature fearful-avoidant trigger, and the one that makes the style hardest to read from outside: activation peaks not during conflict but when the relationship becomes calm, open and loving. If closeness has historically preceded danger, a good stretch is not relief — it is the part just before the turn.

  - triggers → Approach-Avoidance Conflict (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=382)
  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=382)
  - source: How Does A Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @382s — https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=382
